text:
leo: heads up — ran the curl installer on a fresh Ubuntu VM and redwoodctl auth works in a login shell but CI jobs (non-login) can't read tokens. localtest fails with "no credentials". installer put a file in /etc/profile.d/redwood.sh which doesn't get sourced in non-login shells. anyone else hit this?

tara: ah yea, system-wide profile vs env for non-login. what does /etc/profile.d/redwood.sh contain?

leo:
```
# /etc/profile.d/redwood.sh
export REDWOOD_CONFIG=/etc/redwood
export PATH="$PATH:/opt/redwood/bin"
```
but our CI runs via systemd units and Docker ephemeral shells so it never sources /etc/profile.d.

matt: oof. installer probably tried to be "system-wide" for multi-user machines but forgot to drop a drop-in for /etc/environment or a systemd EnvironmentFile. quick fixes: 1) add `/etc/redwood/token` to a well-known path the CLI checks, or 2) have the service set REDWOOD_CONFIG, or 3) change installer to append to /etc/environment.

leo: for now I did `echo REDWOOD_CONFIG=/home/ci/.config/redwood >> /etc/environment` and restarted the service — tests pass. but that feels icky.

tara: filing ISSUE: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/478 — summary: installer uses /etc/profile.d which isn't sufficient for non-interactive services. proposal: installer should create `/etc/environment.d/redwood.conf` (systemd environment) and also write a fallback token file to `/var/lib/redwood/token` with secure perms and have CLI check that path.

matt: small nit — perms need to be tight. use `chmod 0640` and chown to a redwood user or root: if we drop token in var, make sure only processes that need it access it. also add a warning in docs about CI and non-login shells.

deploy-bot: redeploy job #882 queued by leo — logs show `redwoodctl: no credentials found (checked $REDWOOD_CONFIG, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME, /var/lib/redwood/token)`

leo: reproduced locally with `sudo -u ci env -i /opt/redwood/bin/redwoodctl auth status` — fails until /etc/environment set. good repro steps for the issue.

tara: I'll pair with infra to add a systemd unit EnvironmentFile and update the installer PR. also adding an e2e test in CI that spins up a container with no user-profile files to ensure non-login shells still work.

leo: thanks, saved me a lot of debugging in the middle of a release. :pray:
